unit.sep: Construct nets,match boundaries,list faces,measure and qualify ideal models.
unit.careers: Illustrative material/design practices;no professional construction/site approval.
unit.focus: Cone/square/rectangular-pyramid nets,sphere/hemisphere,open/closed conical/pyramidfrustums,actual safe models/diameters and bounded applications.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional planner uses verticalheight as slantheight and adds both endfaces to an open-top bucket.
unit.drivingQuestion: Which nets,faces and measurements justify a solid’s surface area? KICD: How solids used in real life?
unit.storylineThread: Cone → squarepyramid → rectangularpyramid → sphere → hemisphere → conefrustum → pyramidfrustum → actualmodels → actualdiameter → application/volumecontrast → audit → independent evidence.
unit.content: Surface area cone, pyramid (square or rectangular base), sphere, frustum; Applications on area of solids
unit.coreCompetencies:
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner uses a cylinder and a cone of the same radius and height to relate volume of a cove to the volume of a cylinder.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner work with peers to model frustums of cones and pyramids both open and closed.
unit.values:
Social Justice: the learner accords equal opportunities when discussing the uses of pyramids and frustums are used
Responsibility: the learner observes safety precautions of others while using locally available materials to model frustums of cones and pyramids.
unit.pcis: Environment and technology: The learner collects and uses locally available materials to model frustums of cones and pyramids for use as a learning resources.

No teaching cards,models,peers,hints or media. Draw labelled nets/face lists,show formulas and square units;round final nonexact areas to2decimalplaces.

sections.title: 1. Cone and pyramid from nets
sections.prompt: For FinalA,draw/describe a compatible cone sector-and-disk net and a square-pyramid net with every counted face labelled. Determine each closed total surface area and explain slantheight versus verticalheight.

sections.title: 2. Sphere and hemisphere counts
sections.prompt: Determine FinalBsphere area,hemispherecurved area and hemisphereclosed total. State exactly which circularface is included,and why an exact flat sphere net or a thick bowl’s total area is not established by these ideal formulas.

sections.title: 3. Two frustums,open and closed
sections.prompt: For FinalCcompute conicalfrustum lateral,closed and open-top-with-bottom areas;label top/bottomradii. For FinalDdraw a face partition and compute closed and open-top areas. Explain why only the declared missing face is omitted.

sections.title: 4. Application,dimensions and actual evidence
sections.prompt: Explain one useful area application and one fit/waste/measurement limitation. Explain why cone/cylinder1/3volumeratio alone cannot determine area ratio. Name one separate actual observation needed to confirm model-making or diameter-measurement skill.
